title: The empty place, the reshimu and the Kav: G-d hides Himself so that the work is ours
overview:
Chapter 13 is the *nimshal* of chapter 12's analogies. The *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* is G-d hiding His essential light so that something that seems separate from Him can exist. But like the teacher who teaches in short, He loses nothing: the infinite light of the Essence is still there and unchanged, and "you can't not see G-d"; you just don't appreciate what you're seeing, like the cow on the eye doctor's card. That light is not even a *makif* on our world: it is like a person's taste, so the world expresses G-d but cannot define Him.

The *reshimu* is the power of the unlimited to limit itself, but it means that everything was removed, like a footprint. Truer likenesses are the craftsman's notes, the mnemonic, the thrown stone and the peace sign: the world looks like a system running on its own. Yet everything comes out of the *reshimu* through the *Kav*, as a house from its blueprint. G-d does not need a blueprint; He makes the world look fixed so that the *avoda* is ours. The purpose of man is to see past the first *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: The empty place: G-d hides His light, but it is still there, unchanged
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* hides G-d's essential light so that something that seems separate from Him can exist and the light can later be revealed in it. But like the teacher who teaches in short, nothing is lost: the infinite light is still there, the darkness is only from our side, and what the *Kav* reveals is the very light that was before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.en: the *nimshal* for everything that we said in chapter 12 about the *tzimtzum* and *reshimu*,

phrases.he: יובן למעלה בכללות ענין הצמצום הנקרא מקום פנוי,
phrases.en: is understood in G-dliness about the *tzimtzum* that's called the *makom panui*; the *tzimtzum* is called the empty place.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת הסתלקות וההעלם לעצמותו כדי שיוכל להיות אחר כך בחינת השפעת אור כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This idea of this *tzimtzum* is that G-d hides His essential light in order to be able to later bring it in and reveal it, so that it should be able to be in our world.

blocks.text: This is the *nimshal* (what an analogy stands for) of everything chapter 12 said about the *tzimtzum* (contraction) and the *reshimu* (the impression left after the tzimtzum), applied to the *tzimtzum* called the *makom panui* (the empty place). An empty place is somewhere you could put something: this first *tzimtzum* let something that appears separate from G-d exist. "He made place where you could put our world." G-d hides His essential light **in order to be able to later bring it in and reveal it** in our world.

phrases.en: But it's not that it's completely hidden.

phrases.he: אלא כמשל הסתלקות והעלם בעצמו, הידיעה של כל העומק והאריכות כששונה דרך קיצור כנ"ל
phrases.en: G-d's light is not completely hidden; it's like a teacher that when he's explaining it simply, he doesn't forget everything that he knew.

blocks.text: Like the teacher who puts aside the deep explanation and feeds it to the student slowly, until he gets everything. **But it's not that it's completely hidden.** A teacher explaining simply does not forget what he knew; neither is G-d's light completely hidden.

So too when G-d creates the world. He created this table; so what happened to G-d? "Look, it's a table." You say, "No, G-d didn't become a table," right? He does not lose His ability by dealing with our world.

phrases.en: If so,

phrases.he: גם אחר כל ההשתלשלות דאבי''ע שעומד במקום פנוי זה,
phrases.en: even after the whole *hishtalshelus* to create the four worlds that stand in this empty place,

phrases.he: הרי בחינת העלם אור העצמות מקיף וסובב לכל השתלשלות דקו
phrases.en: the essence, the *Atzmus Ein Sof*, G-d's essential self-revelation, which means the revelation of G-d exactly the way He is, is still there.

phrases.he: וכמו שהיה אור העצמות קודם הצמצום ממלא את כל החלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הזה
phrases.en: And just like the light of G-d's essence, the revelation of G-d, before the *tzimtzum* filled this place,
so too after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: הרי ישנו לאור העצמיות כמו שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
phrases.en: G-d's light is still completely infinite; there's still a completely infinite revelation of G-d exactly the way He is,

phrases.he: רק שלא נגלה למטה לגבי שפע המקבלים
phrases.en: just that we're not seeing.

phrases.he: אבל לגבי עצמותו אין שינוי בזה כלל
phrases.en: But G-d still sees everything else, and there's no change to Him.

phrases.he: וכמו משל היודע כל האריכות להשיב לשואלו מיד, גם בשעה ששונה לתלמידו בקיצור כו'.
phrases.en: Like somebody that knows the whole *pilpul* of the Gemara: even when he's explaining it simply, in short, if you ask him a question, he'll right away tell you the whole thing.

blocks.text: **If so, even after the whole hishtalshelus** (the chain of descent) of the four worlds standing in this empty place, the *Atzmus Ein Sof* (G-d's essence), the revelation of G-d exactly as He is, **is still there.** It has not gone anywhere.

It is just hidden from us. People ask, "Can you see G-d?" "The real truth is that you can't not see G-d." Whatever you look at, whatever you experience, you are experiencing the *Atzmus Ein Sof*. "Just you don't appreciate what you're seeing. It's really there."

Just as the light of the Essence filled this place before the *tzimtzum*, as *Etz Chaim* says, **so too after the tzimtzum** it is still completely infinite, a revelation of G-d exactly as He is, **just that we're not seeing.** G-d still knows everything He could do.

Choosing to make this one world does not mean He can't make another. Using these ten *sefiros* (the Divine attributes) does not mean He couldn't use another ten, or thirty, or things that aren't even *sefiros*. Really there are infinite *sefiros* and infinite worlds, and all that is still revealed to Him. He revealed to us only one of the possibilities.

**But G-d still sees everything else, and there's no change to Him.** Like someone who knows the whole *pilpul* (Talmudic debate) of the Gemara: explaining it in short, if you ask him a question he right away tells you the whole thing. So if we would *daven* (pray), G-d could right away reveal whatever we needed. "If He would want to, He could show you everything."

phrases.en: This that it says, this is *Tehillim* chapter 19, that G-d makes darkness His concealment,
like it says in the Gemara,
at the beginning there's darkness and afterwards there's light.
This darkness is only for us, but not to G-d.

phrases.he: שנמשך רק מבחינת הרשימו שנשאר אחר ההעלם כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: For us we only get the light out of the *reshimu*, which is darkness, and we have to pull out the light.

blocks.text: As for **G-d makes darkness His concealment** (*Tehillim* chapter 19, as he gives it) and the Sages' "First darkness and then light": the Gemara asks why the goats run ahead of the lambs. Goats are usually black, lambs white; that is the way the world works, **at the beginning there's darkness and afterwards there's light.**

blocks.question: Why does evil start out on the top, and only afterwards is there good?
blocks.text: That is the real question. And this is the way G-d made the world: at first He made a *tzimtzum*, and there is darkness, and only afterwards does He reveal the light.

blocks.title: The puzzle
blocks.text: Our world is like a puzzle: the answer is hidden and it looks impossible, then you think in a new way and pull out the answer. Everything around us is really a revelation of G-d, but it looks completely hidden, and we have to pull it out.

**This darkness is only for us, but not to G-d.** He still sees the solution to the puzzle. We get the light only out of the *reshimu* left after the hiding, which is darkness, and we have to pull the light out.

phrases.he: וזהו אתה קדוש ושמך, אור העצמי, קדוש ומובדל
phrases.en: This is what it means that You are holy and Your name is holy.
that You are He before He created the world, and You are He after He created the world.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי כו'
phrases.en: I am G-d, I do not change.
why is it the same?
this that G-d reveals deep things from the darkness,
and the concealment,
out from this *reshimu*, out from this concealment, G-d reveals the *hishtalshelus* to us in the *Kav*,

phrases.he: הוא דווקא מאותו אור העצמות שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: That revelation is really the original light from before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.text: This is **You are holy and Your name is holy.** G-d's essence stays above the whole *hishtalshelus*, unaffected; and even His name, His light, stays holy and removed, untouched by the *tzimtzum*, still in its full, original state to G-d. From G-d's point of view the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal).

**You are He before He created the world, and You are He after He created the world.** *Ata* (you) is second person, said to someone who is here; *hu* (he) is third person. *Ata* is the revelation, *hu* the concealment: the revelation of Your essence is the same before the *tzimtzum* and after it.

Just as the infinite light before the *tzimtzum* revealed G-d's essence, so the revelation we see now that He created the world is also a revelation of His essence. As it says, **I am G-d, I do not change.** The *Ani* (I) also represents *Malchus* (kingship): the revelation of G-d does not change. We see it as different, but it is still the same revelation of Him.

Why the same? Because what G-d reveals afterwards **from the darkness** and the concealment, in the shining of the *Kav* (the ray of light), the *hishtalshelus* He reveals to us out of this *reshimu*, comes specifically from the same light of the Essence that was before the *tzimtzum*.

blocks.title: The Gemara pulled out of the Mishna
blocks.text:
**That revelation is really the original light from before the tzimtzum**, like the Gemara we pull out of the Mishna. The Mishna was set up so they could reconstitute whatever they forgot, and what we reconstitute is the same Gemara they had, the original *sechel* (intellect).

So too, though we perceive G-d only through this world, when we find G-dliness in it we get the same revelation there was before the *tzimtzum*.

sections.title: Not a makif on a pnimi: the Essence is not defined by our world
sections.summary: The light of the Essence around the chain is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*, the way the general *makif* of the *Kav* surrounds the four worlds; it is not even in the category of a light that is given. Like a person's taste, it affects everything without relating to any one thing: our world expresses G-d, but G-d cannot be defined by our world.

phrases.he: ואמנם לא נקרא אור העצמות שמקיף ההשתלשלות שבמקום פנוי כו', כמו בחינת מקיף לפנימי,
phrases.en: But nevertheless, even though the light that comes out in our *hishtalshelus* is coming from the revelation of G-d, we don't say that the light of G-d's essence is like a *makif* for the *hishtalshelus* in a way of *makif l'pnimi*.

phrases.he: כמקיף הכללי דקו שמקיף לאבי''ע בשוה כו'
phrases.en: unlike the general *makif* of the *Kav*, which surrounds *ABYA* equally, which is a *makif* on the *pnimi*.

blocks.text: Even so, though the light in our *hishtalshelus* comes from the revelation of G-d, the light of the Essence is not called a *makif* (encompassing light) of the *hishtalshelus* in the way of a *makif l'pnimi*, a *makif* on something inner.

blocks.title: Ice cream, a light bulb, a movie camera
blocks.text: A *makif l'pnimi*, explained later, is like a person who wants ice cream. The desire is general, including every particular step to get it, but it already relates to a certain goal and is somewhat defined by it. Or a light bulb, built specially to give off light; or a movie camera, its lens built transparent for a specific purpose.

blocks.title: A person's taste
blocks.text: Here it is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*; it is like a person's taste. Taste affects everything he does: the flavor of his ice cream, even the kind of cone; in building a house, everything "down to the bathroom drapes." But it relates to no one detail more than another.

blocks.title: The house and the sky
blocks.text: So it surrounds it and is the real cause, but does not relate directly to it. A person's house is a *makif* on a *pnimi*: built specifically to be his, and he directs and controls it. The sky is a *makif* not on a *pnimi*; it does not really relate to you: "if it's going to rain, it's going to rain." A *makif* on a *pnimi* is tied to something separate and already defined by it.

The *makif* not on a *pnimi* means G-d can reveal Himself in anything; it does not relate specifically to our world. The light before the *tzimtzum* is not His ability to make this world but a revelation of Him as He is, a *hiyuli* (raw potential) that could also come out as our world.

But it's one-way: you can't define G-d by our world, because it is not a *makif* on a *pnimi*. Yet our world expresses G-d, because His light is *makif* on it.

It is **unlike the general makif of the Kav**, which surrounds *ABYA* (the four worlds) equally: that is a *makif* on the *pnimi*. The general *makif* after the *tzimtzum*, *sovev kol almin* (the light that encompasses all worlds), is G-dliness as it relates to our world: the ten *sefiros*, G-d's ability to be a Creator. The Essence does not relate specifically to our world.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 31 opens by finishing line 14, which class 30 read at its end.

phrases.he: כי הרי עדיין אינו בגדר וסוג בחינת אור השפעה כלל,
phrases.en: because the essence, the light before the *tzimtzum*, G-d's self-revelation, doesn't relate at all to be something to be given over.

phrases.he: גם לא להיות בחינת מקיף כו'
phrases.en: You can't even call it like a general thing, like a *makif*.

phrases.he: רק אור העצמות, שהוא בחינת התגלותו כמו שהוא בעצמות
phrases.en: The light is just a revelation of G-d exactly as He is.

blocks.text: For the Essence, G-d's self-revelation before the *tzimtzum*, does not relate at all to being given over. Like the power of movement, which has no particular movements in it because it is not in the realm of movement. **You can't even call it like a general thing, like a makif.**
It is **just a revelation of G-d exactly as He is.** As was said of the *hiyuli*: "It's not coats, it's not shoes, it's not a power of movement, it's just Him."

phrases.en: therefore we say,
He endures
and His name endures,
yet we also say, blessed be He and blessed be His name.

phrases.he: רק מבחינת אותיות דגליף בטהירו עילאה זה,
phrases.en: The revelation of our world is coming only from what G-d estimated in the *tehiru ila'a*, in the *glif glifu*, in *Kadmon*,

phrases.he: שהוא מה ששיער בעצמו בכח כו'
phrases.en: which is what G-d estimated in potential, how He wants it to be.

phrases.he: וגם זה הוא הנשאר בבחינת העלם והסתלקות קצת
phrases.en: But even this estimation, even that that was estimated, the *tzimtzum* also hid that,

phrases.he: דהיינו רק לפי ערך אופן הנצרך להשתלשלות אחר צמצום זה
phrases.en: and it's only revealed according to what is needed for this *tzimtzum*, but it's not fully revealed,

blocks.text:
Therefore we say **He endures and His name endures**: even after the *tzimtzum* they are still found. And we say **blessed be He and blessed be His name**: G-d's essence is brought down and revealed within our *hishtalshelus*.

But the revelation in our world comes only from what G-d estimated in potential in the *tehiru ila'a* (the upper purity), the *glif glifu* (the engraving), *Kadmon*: how He wants it to be. Like taste, to be explained later, which influences every detail but was not estimated for this thing specifically. "We'll talk about it later."
**But even this estimation** the *tzimtzum* also hid. It is **only revealed according to what is needed for this tzimtzum**, not fully, *v'dai l'mevin* (and this is enough for one who understands).

That was the *nimshal* of the teacher and the student. First, as the teacher does not forget, G-d did not change or lose His ability; He still knows who He is. "He didn't like, 'Oh no, I'm a table!' He's not like having an identity crisis or something." Second, as the teacher sees the whole Gemara in the Mishna, G-d sees the full revelation of His essence in the world.

If you know how to look into anything in the world, a table, a pear, and study it, you will find G-d there, the whole infinite Essence. And though to us it looks hidden because of the *reshimu*, we can work to pull out the light until we find the original light of the Essence, because it is really there. We don't appreciate what we're seeing; but we are seeing it.

blocks.title: The eye doctor's card
blocks.text:
Rabbi Walters used to go on *mivtzaim* (outreach) with an eye doctor whose business card had a black and white picture on the back: "What am I?" You see nothing. "Come on, don't you see? So simple!" "First of all, you're holding it the wrong way," and he turns it. Still nothing. "It's a cow." You squint; no cow. Then he points: "This is the eye, this is the ear, this is the nose, this is the body, it's the fence." All of a sudden it clicks: a photograph of a cow standing in a field.

Your mind didn't register it because of the way the things came together. But once it clicks, for the rest of your life you'll see a cow right away.

So with the world: the whole time you're seeing G-d, it just doesn't click. *Chassidus*, the Torah, the *mitzvos*, making a *birur* (refinement) of the sparks: "It's just to put in the order." You see what this is and what that is, how it all fits together, and suddenly, "Oh!", you realize you are looking at G-d.

sections.title: The soul and the body: connected, yet not changed
sections.summary: By the second *mashal*, the soul's life in the body: the soul is bound to the body and affected by it, yet it loses nothing when a limb fails. So the light of the Essence shines after the *tzimtzum*, connected to the measured revelation of the *Kav*, and is not changed by it. All the *meshalim* come to one point.

phrases.he: וגם על פי אופן משל הב' הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: also according to the second *mashal*,
the consciousness of the soul that's in the body,

phrases.he: שמשתנה ממהות רוחני למהות גשמי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that it changes from being spiritual in nature and essence to being physical,

phrases.he: גם כן אין זה שינוי כלל,
phrases.en: This is also not a real change,

phrases.he: שהרי כמו שיש קישור וחיבור לחיות הגשמי לחיות הרוחני
phrases.en: just like there is a bond and a connection between the physical consciousness and the spiritual consciousness,

phrases.he: ממה שרואים התפעלות הנפש ממקרי חיות הגוף,
phrases.en: like we see that the soul is affected by what happens to the body.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה לא ישתנה בעצם הרוחנית מחסרון התפשטות חיות אבר גשמי כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: And on the other hand, it's not affected if something happens to the physical body.

phrases.he: כך אין שינוי בבחינת אור העצמות, להיותו מאיר גם אחר הצמצום
phrases.en: So too, even when G-d shines, reveals Himself after the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: גם שאינו רק לפי ערך ההשתלשלות
phrases.en: and even though after the *tzimtzum* G-d reveals Himself in a way of *memalei*, individualized according to the proportion and the relationship of the *hishtalshelus*,
nevertheless, even though it's being revealed in a limited way after the *tzimtzum*, it's still connected to the *Atzmus* of the light before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בצמצום האור בבחינת הקו,
phrases.en: even though it comes in a measured way,

phrases.he: אין זה שינוי כלל באור העצמות על פי משל זה
phrases.en: So there's no real change in the light of the *Atzmus*, based on this *mashal*.

blocks.text: That was the *nimshal* of the first *mashal*, the teacher. Now the second, the life of the soul and the body: **the consciousness of the soul that's in the body**, which **changes from being spiritual in nature and essence to being physical**.

**This is also not a real change**: the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto*, and by this *mashal* creating the world is no real change in G-d. There is **a bond and a connection between the physical consciousness and the spiritual consciousness**: the soul is affected by what happens to the body. The real consciousness in the body, what perceives and gets happy and sad, is the soul.

So the essence of the soul connects to the body and is revealed in it, not fully. **And on the other hand, it's not affected if something happens to the physical body.** If the eye is ruined, G-d forbid, the soul does not lose its power of sight.

So too when G-d reveals Himself after the *tzimtzum*: this table reveals G-d, but if I burn the table I am not hurting G-d.

After the *tzimtzum* G-d reveals Himself as *memalei* (filling), measured to the proportion of the *hishtalshelus*, yet still connected to the Essence before the *tzimtzum*. Coming in measure, there is *hispaalus* (being affected), so to speak: He answers our prayers, something holy reveals Him more and the revelation can go away, measure for measure. But that is only how it is after. **So there's no real change in the light of the Atzmus, based on this mashal.**

phrases.he: וכן על פי משל הג' מכח התנועה בגשם או כמשל התחכמות מכח המשכיל הנזכר לעיל

phrases.en: it all comes up to one general point,

blocks.text: So too by the third *mashal*, the power of movement in the body, or intellect in the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight): **it all comes up to one general point.** From G-d's side the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto*: making the world does not lessen Him, and in it He sees a full revelation of Himself. From our side the full revelation is there too; we just don't appreciate it. When we pray, G-d Himself answers. And yet it is no change.

sections.title: The reshimu is the power of limitation in the unlimited light
sections.summary: The *reshimu*, compared above to the short version that includes the whole length, is in G-dliness the *koach hahagbala*: the power of the unlimited light to bring all of itself, limited, into one impression, even into a speck of dust. G-d can do anything, and so He can also limit.

phrases.en: the *reshimu* that was explained previously,

phrases.he: שזהו כמו הקיצור שכלול בו כל האריכות
phrases.en: which is like the summary that includes the whole *arichus*, like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara,

phrases.he: הנה למעלה יובן מזה שזהו בחינת כח ההגבלה שיש באור אין סוף הבלתי מוגבל בעצם
phrases.en: But *reshimu* in the *nimshal* is the power of limitation that exists in the *Or Ein Sof*, which is essentially not limited.

phrases.he: דהיינו להביא כל הארות אור העצמות הבלתי גבול בבחינת הגבול
phrases.en: In other words, the power of the light is to reveal G-d; the power of the *reshimu* is to reveal G-d in a limited way.
that's the idea of the impression,

phrases.he: שכולל בבחינת הגבלה מבחינת כל עצמות אור אין סוף,
phrases.en: that it includes in a limited way the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*,
like the *kitzur* that includes everything, like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara.

blocks.text: So now comes the *nimshal* for the *reshimu*: **the reshimu that was explained previously**, which is like the summary that includes the whole length, **like the way the Mishna includes the Gemara**.

In the *nimshal* the *reshimu* is the *koach hahagbala*, the power of limitation in the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light), which in itself is unlimited. **The power of the light is to reveal G-d; the power of the reshimu is to reveal G-d in a limited way**: to put the whole *gilui* (revelation) of the Essence into an infinitely little speck of dust on this table. "G-d could do that, right?"

**That's the idea of the impression**: it includes, limited, the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*, like the *kitzur* (shortening) that includes everything, the way the Mishna includes the Gemara: very short, but it's in there. However small anything is, G-d packs the whole Essence into it, and if you studied even the tiniest particle properly, you would find it there.

phrases.en: because G-d can do anything; He's omnipotent,

phrases.he: וכלול בו גם כן מכח המגביל
phrases.en: He also has the power to limit.

phrases.he: להגביל ולכלול ברשימה א' מכל אור העצמות כו'
phrases.en: So He also has the power to limit and to include in a single impression, in a single point, all the light of the *Atzmus*.

blocks.text: **Because G-d can do anything; He's omnipotent,** He also has the power to limit, and "he can do a really good job": take something infinite and reveal it in an infinitesimal way, including all the light of the *Atzmus* in a single impression, a single point, as explained elsewhere at length. That is the main *nimshal*.

But the *mashal* of the *kitzur*, the Mishna, is not really a good one for the *reshimu*. The other *meshalim* (analogies) will show that in the *nimshal* it is more limited still: not just that G-d made it very dense, but even more than that.

sections.title: Truer likenesses: the craftsman's mark, the mnemonic, the thrown stone, the hint
sections.summary: The *reshimu* means that everything was taken away, like a footprint when the foot is gone, so the short version is not a true likeness. Truer are the craftsman's line, the mnemonic, and most of all the thrown stone, whose force is hidden in it and in the arm, and the hand's sign or the writing that hides an idea: the world looks separate and self-running, and G-d's involvement is hidden in it.

phrases.he: אך הנה באמת אין זה דמיון אמיתי לבחינת הרשימו הנשאר בחלל ריקן ומקום פנוי הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: This *mashal*, this comparison to the *kitzur*, is not the proper comparison for the *reshimu* that's left over in this empty place.

phrases.he: כי הוא מורה שנסתלק משם הכל
phrases.en: because the idea of the *reshimu* indicates that everything was removed; that doesn't mean that it was just made very condensed, it means that it's not there.

phrases.he: ולא שנשאר איזה אור רק שהוא בקצור וגבול,
phrases.en: and not that there was some light left, there's a little bit of a revelation, it's just very condensed,

phrases.he: אלא רק בחינת רשימו בעלמא כו'
phrases.en: but only an impression, meaning that the original thing was taken away, like a footprint; the foot's gone.

blocks.text: The *kitzur* is not the true comparison for the *reshimu* left in this empty place, because a *reshimu* means everything was removed: not some light left, very condensed, but only an impression, the original taken away. Like a footprint: **the foot's gone.**

phrases.he: אם כן הדמיון האמיתי הוא מרושם וציון קו קצר שעושין האומנין, שכולל כל אריכות מעשה הבנין
phrases.en: So if so, a better *mashal* is like the little blueprint or the little notes that a craftsman makes for how to build the entire thing,
even more than this,
like a mnemonic,
so too in G-dliness,

phrases.he: כתיב זכר רב טובך, העצמי כו'
phrases.en: that our world is only like a *zecher*, is only like a remembrance of G-d's abundant goodness.
and the like.

blocks.title: The craftsman's notes
blocks.text: The true likeness is **the little blueprint or the little notes that a craftsman makes for how to build the entire thing.** The Mishna explains the Gemara; here there is no explanation, "it's just like some line." Yet from it you know how to build the whole thing.

**Even more than this**, it is like a mnemonic, where it is completely hidden. **So too in G-dliness**: "Remember Your abundant goodness"; our world is only like a remembrance of G-d's abundant goodness, like the letters of a mnemonic, **and the like.**

The *reshimu* means G-d makes the world with His light completely hidden. That is why we don't see Him: naturally a person feels he sees a physical world, not G-d. His revelation is not direct but like a mnemonic or a blueprint, a foreign thing that hints at it. A table, because it was created, hints that there is a Creator; but we see a hint, not the Creator.

phrases.he: ויותר בהעלם והסתלקות הוא כמשל הזורק אבן כו' כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: Or even more so is like the *mashal* of throwing a stone, which is the main *mashal* of the *reshimu*.
like it says in *Sefer HaBahir*,
like it was thrown.

phrases.he: שהרי בחינת הרשימו נשאר נבדל בריחוק מקום מעצמות האור וכו'
phrases.en: because the *reshimu* is left so that it seems like it's distant from the *Atzmus HaOr*,
And the power that's hidden within this *reshimu* is called

phrases.he: בחינת העלם אור, נבדל מהעלם עצמות האור דאין סוף
phrases.en: the concealment of the light, which is separate from the essential concealment of the light of the *Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: כמו כח נבדל הנעלם בזריקת אבן
phrases.en: Like when you throw a stone: there's a power of movement, there's a force that's hidden now within the stone,

phrases.he: שבא מכח היד שכבר נעלם בעצמו כו'
phrases.en: And also in the person's arm that threw it, you don't see the implementation of his force.

blocks.text: **Or even more so** it is like throwing a stone, the main *mashal* of the *reshimu*; *Sefer HaBahir* says **like it was thrown.** The *reshimu* seems far from the Essence of the light, and so our world looks thrown: we don't see G-d's involvement so much.

Not that it actually is so; but we can look at the world as thrown, as if G-d made it once and now it goes on its own. "Like there was a big bang, and it sent everything flying, and now it's going." The physical world looks as if it left the realm of G-dliness altogether; being a natural system makes it look independent.

The power hidden in this *reshimu* is called **the concealment of the light, which is separate from the essential concealment of the light of the Ein Sof.** Like the separate power in a thrown stone, which came from the hand: a force is now hidden in the stone; you don't see it applied, only that the stone moves. **And also in the person's arm that threw it, you don't see the implementation of his force**: just his arm at rest. The movement is hidden in his arm and hidden in the stone.

Why "separate from the concealment of the Essence"? Because it is hidden two ways, as in the stone and in the arm: hidden within the world, and G-d's involvement hidden too. He seems to sit back and watch while the world goes on its own; unless there are miracles, we don't see G-d's hand, so to speak.

That the world can look like a separate system is the main thing of the *tzimtzum*: G-d looks uninvolved, and that makes us feel independent from Him.

phrases.en: like all the orbits and stars, or the planets and the stars,
that are moving from G-d's power of movement,

phrases.he: הנעלם, שבא בבחינת זריקה מאור וכח האלה״י
phrases.en: which is hidden within them, from G-d's power of throwing,
the *chitzoniyus* nine *kelim* of *Malchus d'Asiya*,

phrases.he: שנקרא זה כח הנבדל בחינת מלכות שבמלכות
phrases.en: once they're actually thrown, that is called *Malchus sheb'Malchus*,
which *Malchus sheb'Malchus* is where it becomes far from you,

phrases.he: ולא כמו הכתיבה באצבע או כח יד הפועל עצמו בנפעל
phrases.en: and not like when you're writing or when you're moving something with your hand,
when you're actually moving something directly with your hand, that's the revelation of your power in a way that's close, that you see the connection.
That's just plain *Malchus*.

blocks.text: So too the *galgalim* (the celestial orbits), the planets and stars, moving by G-d's power of movement hidden in them, His power of throwing: He actually set them moving. That power is **the chitzoniyus nine kelim** (the outer nine vessels) **of Malchus d'Asiya**, which move the whole universe; the nine planets correspond to the nine *kelim*.

Once they are actually thrown, that separate power is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*. The power of movement while still connected is the first nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*: holding something and moving it is plain *Malchus*; throwing it, so it is separate from your power, is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*.

All these levels exist; it depends on what you perceive. Realizing that every single moment G-d moves the world and the planets is the nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*. Seeing them as just thrown, "and maybe G-d threw it, you know, once upon a time, but now, you know, Big Bang and then it's just going," is *Malchus sheb'Malchus*: set flying.

That is the *reshimu*: you don't see G-d's involvement directly, but since He did it you can look into it and find a hint of Him, "like graphology or something." *Malchus sheb'Malchus* **is where it becomes far from you**, unlike writing or moving something with your hand, where you see the connection: **That's just plain Malchus**, as explained elsewhere at length.

He remarks that a parenthesis seems to be missing after "as explained elsewhere at length", or else the one before it should not be there.

phrases.en: and *meshalim* that are even closer for this, the idea of the *reshimu*,
like a hint with a hand motion for a *sechel*.
The movement lifting those two fingers hints at a whole thing, but the *sechel* is completely hidden there.

phrases.he: שזהו נקרא בחינת הלבשה ותפיסא בדבר נבדל כו'
phrases.en: That is the idea that it changes its *mahus*: it's being represented by something, it's enclothed in something different, and it's being expressed by that.

phrases.he: וכן כשכותב שכל וחכמה בתנועת האצבע כו'
phrases.en: Same thing when you're writing: there the intellect goes through the hand, and it's hidden, but then it comes out through being on paper.

blocks.title: The peace sign
blocks.text: Even closer *meshalim*: **a hint with a hand motion for a sechel**, the idea hidden in a physical movement. "Like a peace sign, right?" Lifting two fingers hints at a whole thing, but the *sechel* is completely hidden; a person sees a movement, not intellect.

So we look and see just a physical world, no meaning. "Yeah, that's because you don't understand the language." You see fingers; in the *nimshal*, the trees and the tables and the sky. "Well, I don't see G-d." "Yeah, that's because you don't understand how this is a symbol for what this represents."
This is called being enclothed and grasped in a separate thing: **it changes its mahus** (what a thing is in itself). It is enclothed in something different and expressed by it.

blocks.title: G-d writing His autobiography
blocks.text: **Same thing when you're writing**: the intellect goes through the hand, hidden, and comes out on paper. So here physical movements and physical things are a language: G-d is writing, "as He's writing His autobiography," and the changes we see in the world are the changes on the paper.

That is how revelation comes out of the *reshimu* again: seeing the differences between things reveals it. At first it is hidden as a physical movement, but there is intellect there; the *reshimu* is the written thing, the movement of the hand, with the intellect completely hidden.

Take the world at face value, everything individual and unconnected, and you see no meaning. But see how it all fits together, as the next chapter explains, and there is a language, though no single letter on the paper means anything. "We'll talk about that next chapter."

phrases.he: כך למעלה, בחינת הרשימו בחינת דבר נבדל בערך,
phrases.en: so too, *reshimu* is the idea that reality seems like something that's separate from G-dliness.

phrases.he: שבו מלובש בהעלם מכללות אור העצמות כו'
phrases.en: but nevertheless, really the whole light of G-d is hidden within our world, and if we'll look into it, we'll be able to find it.

blocks.text: So too above, the *reshimu* means **reality seems like something that's separate from G-dliness.** We perceive a physical created world as separate: the table is not G-d, it's a table. "That's the whole thing of *avoda zara*" (idol worship): "what, that's not G-d, this is a world, right?"

And G-d's involvement in it is hidden too. So it is both: He is revealed through something that seems separate from Him, and there is a change of *mahus*, from G-dly and infinite to physical and limited. **But nevertheless, really the whole light of G-d is hidden within our world, and if we'll look into it, we'll be able to find it.** "And that's what we're going to try to do."

sections.title: Everything comes from the reshimu: nothing is missing from You
sections.summary: Though everything was removed and the light remains in the *reshimu* only hidden, short and hinted, or as a thrown, separate power, all the details of the *Kav* come from it, because it includes everything. It holds what G-d estimated in *Kadmon*, seen in one glance; so all that is formed is not missing "from You".

phrases.en: however, from all of these *meshalim* together,

phrases.he: יובן על כל פנים כללות ענין הרשימו
phrases.en: it's at least understood, the general *inyan* of the *reshimu*.

phrases.he: דגם שהוא בא בבחינת הסתלקות הכל,
phrases.en: that even though the *reshimu* comes in a way where everything is removed,

phrases.he: ולא נשאר בה רק בהעלם גדול
phrases.en: the original light only remains in the *reshimu* in a very hidden way,
it's completely short and just hinted at,
or it can also be looked at in a little bit different way: it's like something that was thrown, that it's now seen as something that's separate and outside from the self.
nevertheless,

phrases.he: מזה עצמו בא ונמשך כל פרטי ההשתלשלות דקו
phrases.en: from this itself, from this *reshimu* itself, comes all the details of what comes on into the *Kav*, through the *Kav*.
it all comes from this *reshimu*.
because in this little impression,

phrases.he: להיותה כוללת הכל בהעלם על כל פנים,
phrases.en: since it includes everything, albeit in a very hidden way,

phrases.he: היא הנותנת שיוכל לבא הכל בהתגלות על ידי בחינת הקו
phrases.en: this is what gives the possibility that everything should be able to come out from it, should be revealed from it through the *Kav*,
everything in *hishtalshelus* until the end of *Asiya*, the physical world.

blocks.text: Having given the *nimshal* of each *mashal* of the *reshimu*, now the general idea. From them all **it's at least understood, the general inyan** (concept) of the *reshimu*: everything is removed and the original light remains in it only very hidden, **it's completely short and just hinted at.** Or, seen a little differently, it is like something thrown, now seen as separate and outside the self.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 33 opens by summing up the meshalim of lines 34-53 before it reads line 54.

blocks.text: **Nevertheless**, hidden and short as the original light is in it, from the *reshimu* itself come all the details of what comes into and through the *Kav*. **It all comes from this reshimu.**

Because this little impression includes everything, however hidden, it is what lets everything come out and be revealed through the *Kav*. Once it is there, the *Kav* can pull it out. How, when that seems very hard or impossible, the next chapter explains. "But once it's there, it's possible to take it back out."

Were it not there at all, it would be *tzimtzum kipshuto*, completely hidden for good. Some things, other *sefiros*, don't come out of the *reshimu*, though they are hidden there too and could. Mainly it holds what was estimated in *Kadmon* for the *hishtalshelus*, hidden; deeper, the whole light of the Essence, from which anything can be pulled. The *Kav* draws it out to the end of *Asiya* (the world of Action): **everything in hishtalshelus until the end of Asiya, the physical world.**

phrases.he: וכמאמר כל היצור לא נכחד ממך
phrases.en: like it says that all of what is created, or really *yetzur* means what is formed, is not missing from You.
from You, *davka*, meaning from G-d Himself.

phrases.he: שזהו הכל נעשה ונמשך בגלוי כמו שעלה ברצונו הפשוט בעצמות האור שלפני הצמצום
phrases.en: that everything in the *hishtalshelus* is done according to, is made and is brought out according to the way that it arose in G-d's simple will within Himself,
in the estimation that He made in the light before the *tzimtzum*,

phrases.he: שהרי במחשבה קדומה זו ששיער בעצמו
phrases.en: because in this original thought where He estimated it to Himself, and this we mean *Kadmon* here,

phrases.he: הוא צופה ומביט הכל בסקירה א'
phrases.en: He saw everything from the beginning to the end in one glance.

phrases.he: דהיינו מה שנסקר בהעלם ובקיצור ורמז ברשימו זו כו'
phrases.en: And this whole estimation is what's put into this impression, this *reshimu*, and in this *reshimu*, everything is seen in a hidden and in a very short and hinted way, in one glance.

blocks.text: As it says, all that is formed is not missing from You (*yetzur* means what is formed). **From You, davka** (specifically): from G-d Himself. Everything that comes out in the world comes from G-d Himself.

Everything in the *hishtalshelus* comes out as it arose in G-d's simple will, **in the estimation that He made in the light before the tzimtzum**, in *Kadmon*. In this original thought, which is what *Kadmon* means here, **He saw everything from the beginning to the end in one glance.**
This whole estimation is put into the *reshimu*, where everything is seen hidden, very short and hinted, in one glance. "It's all there." It is like one point, but hidden in it is everything.

sections.title: The craftsman's blueprint: a plan kept so that the work is ours
sections.summary: The craftsman builds the whole house from his outline, which he makes so that he will not deviate or have to think it through again. G-d does not forget; turning the *mashal* around, He makes the world look like a fixed system He set up once, so that the *avoda* falls on us and we feel the responsibility.

phrases.en: and this is like the analogy of the craftsman's blueprint,

phrases.he: שממנו דוקא ידע לעשות כל אריכות מעשה הבנין בפרטי פרטיו
phrases.en: that specifically from looking at the blueprint, the craftsman knows how to make everything: he can build the whole house from the blueprint, with all of its most minute details,
from its beginning to its end.

phrases.he: רק כדי שלא יתעלם ממנו טעמו ונימוקו בעצמותו לאריכות הענין, הוא עושה לו רושם לזכרון
phrases.en: He makes it so that he will not forget the whole reason of why he decided to do it exactly this way.
so that he shouldn't deviate from it,
and he won't have to go think about it again.

blocks.title: The craftsman's blueprint
blocks.text: It is like **the analogy of the craftsman's blueprint**: specifically from the blueprint, the craftsman knows how to build the whole house with all its most minute details, **from its beginning to its end.**

Why make it? To understand a blueprint fully you already need to know a lot, and only its maker really appreciates it, especially when it is not standardized: a craftsman's *roshem* (outline) can be his personal notes that only he understands. **He makes it so that he will not forget the whole reason of why he decided to do it exactly this way**, once he is in the middle of building.

**So that he shouldn't deviate from it, and he won't have to go think about it again.** In the middle of building he forgets: "There's a reason why I wanted to put this here and not there. Cuz now it seems like, oh, it's better to put it there." Then he has to rethink why structurally it won't work, or, "Oh yeah, I forgot, they have to run the plumbing through that way."

Someone who wants to be an architect was just telling Rabbi Walters that besides the engineering that keeps a building sound, they study plumbing, to make room for the pipes, and electricity and other considerations, to know how to take them into account. But while building he doesn't want to think about those things; he just wants to think about how to build it.

phrases.he: וכמו כן ענין הציונים ללימוד עמוק שבעצמו כו'
phrases.en: so too the idea of making little notes, sort of mnemonics, to help you remember a deep subject,

phrases.he: שזהו תועלת לידע מהם כל אורך עיון עומק עצמותו שיש לו, פן ינטה ממנו כו'
phrases.en: and from remembering that, it will remind you the whole *halacha* with all the reasons and everything, and you won't deviate from it.

blocks.title: Notes for a deep subject
blocks.text: **So too the idea of making little notes, sort of mnemonics, to help you remember a deep subject.** After a whole *pilpul* to figure out the *halacha* (the law), you remember a short little thing, like a Mishna or shorter, a mnemonic, and it reminds you of the whole *halacha* with all its reasons, **and you won't deviate from it.**

The *nimshal*: in *Kadmon* G-d estimated everything that will be in the world, "all that is formed is not missing from You": the whole history, down to how many hairs on each person's head, how many feathers on every bird, how many times every blade of grass shakes in the wind. All of it is planned, and must be exactly that way for *Moshiach* to come. That is part of *hashgacha pratis* (divine providence): the world *davka* has to be this way; "G-d likes it this way." Now it is just bringing out what the blueprint planned.

blocks.question: Why would the *mashal* of the blueprint apply to G-d, who is not going to forget or deviate? Why would He need the *reshimu*?
blocks.text:
Going from *mashal* to *nimshal* you always have to fix it. The craftsman makes a blueprint for two reasons: not to have to rethink it, and not to deviate. G-d is not going to go, "Oh, what was it again?", or make a mistake, "Oh, I forgot, yeah."

Of course He doesn't need the *reshimu* and won't forget. Going from *mashal* to *nimshal* you switch it around: put the deficiencies of the *mashal* on us. G-d wants the world to look as if it runs on its own, without His constant involvement.

He wants it to look like a one-time involvement: He figured it all out, and now it goes on its own. Down to the level of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) you still see Him involved, but without reaching into His essence, nothing really new from Him, just following the system He set up. So two things: He seems not to go back into the *omek* (depth), and not to deviate from it, like a system.
And the reason that He wants these two things is that He wants to put the *avoda* (divine service) on us: to make it that we should feel that G-d set up the world a certain way.

blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab's oath
blocks.text:
There is a story, they say, that the Rebbe Rashab made G-d swear that when the *bochurim* (young yeshiva students) learning *Chassidus* understand the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of descending worlds) wrong, He would not change it to make them right, so that they would have to work to understand it right.

That is the *reshimu*'s "lest he deviate from it": that He should not change from it.

G-d makes a commitment with Himself, so to speak, to run the world a certain way. Not changing from it gives us our *avoda* and makes it matter that we do things *davka* this way: He wants *Moshiach* to come like this, and He won't let us off without reaching that goal. "So that's one of the things that makes it hard."

He also wants it to look as if it no longer comes every moment from His *etzem* (essence). If you saw it always coming straight from G-d's choice, it wouldn't look like a system; it would look as if every moment He is just deciding what He wants to do.

blocks.title: The teacher's class plan
blocks.text: Like a teacher who sets up a system of reward and punishment, grading and class requirements, planned beforehand: accomplish these things or you're not going to pass. He wants it to look like something outside him that he just works within. Otherwise you feel no weight on you: "Oh, he's just doing whatever he wants," so you can just ask him to be nice and change it.

And really, when we *daven* we do ask G-d to be nice and change it, and sometimes He does. But unless we go past this level, the *tzimtzum* He set up makes us have to do *avoda* and feel that it is our responsibility.

sections.title: The reshimu as the source of the Kav: the point and the vav
sections.summary: Like the blueprint, the *reshimu* holds the whole light hidden and is the source of everything in the *Kav*, so the whole chain looks like a set system following one plan. It is the point with two opposites, hiding what is above it and revealing everything to those below; the *Kav* drawn from it is the *vav* whose head is a *yud*, narrower than its source.

phrases.he: וכך בחינת הרשימו הזאת הכוללת ברמז ובקיצור מכל אור העצמות הנעלם בה,
phrases.en: So just like the blueprint, so too this *reshimu* includes in it, in a hinted, in a *kitzur* way, the whole light of the *Atzmus*, which is hidden in it.

phrases.he: הוא עצמו המקור לכל ההמשכות דקו וחוט
phrases.en: This *reshimu* itself is the source for everything that comes out in the *Kav*.
both the *makifim* of the *hishtalshelus* and the *pnimi* of the *hishtalshelus*, from its beginning all the way to its end,

phrases.he: שיהיה הכל כמו שעלה ברצונו וחכמתו הפשוטה בעצמות אור אין סוף ממש כו'
phrases.en: that it should all be according to the way that He originally wanted, with His will and His wisdom, simple will and wisdom, in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*.

blocks.text: **So just like the blueprint**, the *reshimu* includes, hinted and short, the whole light of the Essence hidden in it, and **this reshimu itself is the source for everything that comes out in the Kav.** Everything in the rest of the *hishtalshelus* comes through this *tzimtzum* and is defined by the *reshimu*; this step makes everything else the way it is.

And it looks thrown: as if G-d set up a certain *hishtalshelus* and now it goes. That is why Kabbala looks to many people "like it's this machine or something," a system: G-d made it a set thing, and from that level down we understand Him through the system He set up.

This holds for the *makifim* (encompassing lights) and the *pnimi* (inner light) of the *hishtalshelus*, **from its beginning all the way to its end**: everything comes out by the *reshimu*, so **it should all be according to the way that He originally wanted**, with His simple will and wisdom in *Atzmus Or Ein Sof mamash*. The *hishtalshelus* looks like it follows a one-time plan that G-d decided.

phrases.en: this is what is explained elsewhere,
that a point, which the *reshimu* is compared to a point, has two aspects to it. It has concealment and revelation,
two opposites, two opposite things.

phrases.he: העלם מכל מה שעליון הימנה בערך,
phrases.en: that the point, the *reshimu*, is a concealment of everything that's higher than it, relative to it.
and it's the source of the revelation of everything to the recipients.
It all comes out from it.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הקו שנמשך מן הרשימו
phrases.en: and the revelation that comes to the recipients is the *Kav* that comes from the *reshimu*,
the relationship of the *Kav* to the *reshimu* is like the letter *vav*;
the head of it is a *yud*, which represents the *reshimu*: it's a point,
and then from that point it's drawn down,
as explained elsewhere at length, how the *Kav* is drawn out from the *reshimu*.

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, a point (*nekuda*), and the *reshimu* is compared to one, has concealment and revelation, **two opposites, two opposite things.** It is **a concealment of everything that's higher than it, relative to it**: the whole *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* is put into it so short and hinted that you don't see it there. **And it's the source of the revelation of everything to the recipients**: the whole *gilui* they get comes from it.

blocks.title: A funnel, and CliffNotes
blocks.text: Like a funnel: it takes everything from above and channels it down, and it all comes out. So the Mishna is a short little thing, "like CliffNotes or something," of the way Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi knew the Gemara; for us it is the source of the whole Gemara.

The revelation to the recipients is the *Kav* drawn from the *reshimu*, shaped like the letter *vav*, whose head is a *yud*: the *yud* is the *reshimu*, a point, and from it the line is drawn down, **as explained elsewhere at length, how the Kav is drawn out from the reshimu.**

Look at the *vav*: its line is thinner than the *yud*, which, though a point, has a little width. That is because the *Kav* is less than the *reshimu*. The *reshimu* is a point from the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite), like a zero, but "the nothing of the *reshimu* is bigger than everything in our *hishtalshelus*," and the whole *Kav* is smaller than it.

What comes on the *Kav* never brings out everything hidden in the *reshimu*. Like the Mishna: the whole Gemara explains it, yet there is more in the Mishna, and you can pull out more and more forever. So this world comes out of the *reshimu*, but from the same *roshem* totally different worlds could come out too, as explained elsewhere at length.

sections.title: Summing up: G-d limits Himself so that all is revealed, and the purpose of man is to see past it
sections.summary: The *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav* are G-d limiting Himself, so to speak, so that this world can be revealed; He hid everything else He could do, and the choosing is itself a revelation. From His own light comes a born light, the *Kav*, like a glowing sheet of metal. The whole of man is to feel this deeply and see past the first *tzimtzum*, and so be bound to G-d Himself.

phrases.he: ובכל זה מובן כללות ענין הצמצום דמקום פנוי
phrases.en: From all of this, we understand the general *inyan* of the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui*, the empty place *tzimtzum*,
and the impression that was left,
and also the line which comes out from the *reshimu*,

phrases.he: שהוא רק בחינת הגבלה בעצמות כדי שיומשך הכל בגלוי
phrases.en: That the general idea of the *tzimtzum*, *reshimu*, and the *Kav* is that G-d limits Himself, so to speak, in order that everything should be brought out in a revealed way.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
phrases.en: This is what it says: With You is the source of life,
and from Your light is seen light,
a born light,
which is the idea of the *Kav*.
like will be explained with the help of G-d,

blocks.text: From all this the general idea of the *tzimtzum* of the *makom panui* is understood: the *tzimtzum* that let it appear that there is something separate from G-d. An empty place is one where you can put something, and to put things there you must empty the space; so He hid Himself. **And the impression that was left, and also the line which comes out from the reshimu**: the next two chapters explain these.

The *tzimtzum*, *reshimu* and *Kav* together mean that **G-d limits Himself, so to speak, in order that everything should be brought out in a revealed way.** To reveal the world as it is now, He hid everything else He could do: different worlds, different *sefiros*, a completely different way.

But He did not lose His potential, and it is a complete revelation of Him. In a way a greater one: you see Him choosing how it should be, and choosing that it be *davka* this way is itself a *gilui* of Him. That is one way the *tzimtzum* itself is a *gilui*.

This is **With You is the source of life**; from Your light is seen light. From Your light, the light of the *Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, the revelation of G-d Himself, is seen a different light, *or shel tolda*, **a born light**, which is the *Kav*: a light that is just induced.

blocks.title: The curtain and the glowing metal
blocks.text: A very strong light shining on a curtain: you don't see the original light, just a new light coming through. Better in a way: a very strong light on an iron curtain, a sheet of metal no light can pass. It heats the metal, which glows with a new light. The glow shows there must be a light behind it, and where it glows brighter shows where the light is concentrated. But you don't see the original at all.

So too, because of the *tzimtzum* we look at the world and see a *gilui* of *chachma* (wisdom) and *middos* (emotional attributes), but not of G-d Himself. Through *avoda* we go past the *tzimtzum* and reveal Him too; that is its purpose, that we have to work to uncover that level, and that is why we have to make a *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below). **Like will be explained with the help of G-d**, how the *Kav* works.

phrases.en: and this is the whole purpose of man.
to really become very sensitive for this whole idea, that it should really hit you,
and similar things, meaning the rest of the *hishtalshelus* that we're going to explain the rest of the book,

phrases.he: מפני שמזה דוקא יבוא לכלל היחוד האמיתי בהתקשרות נפשו בחיי כל החיים העליונים, שהוא עצמות אור אין סוף ממש מטעם הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין:

blocks.text: This is **the whole purpose of man**: to deepen his *daas* (knowledge) in this, **to really become very sensitive for this whole idea, that it should really hit you.** To feel how everything in the *hishtalshelus* is nothing, just G-d holding Himself back and revealing a little of what He can do; to feel how it really comes from G-d Himself, and see past the first *tzimtzum*.

That is the main purpose of our *avoda*: to see past the first *tzimtzum*. Even if he does not *mamash* (actually) see past it, a person should live with this *daas*, really feel it, so that what he connects to and feels is important is G-d Himself. Everything else should not impress him: only a means to an end, with no intrinsic importance.

With that attitude a person goes with a high hand: nothing impresses him, not the world, not even *Gan Eden* (Paradise) and *Olam Haba* (the World to Come). He just does his *shlichus* (mission), what G-d tells him to do. **And similar things**: the rest of the *hishtalshelus*, explained in the rest of the book; one should see through all the *tzimtzumim*, but in a way this is the main one.

Only by developing a sensitivity to see past the concealment G-d set up in the world does a person come to the true union. That hiding makes things look set: there is a *teva* (nature), you work within its framework and its limits, and so you can't always do Torah and *mitzvos*, "you have to worry about this, you have to worry about that." Seeing past these limits is what lets us connect to G-d: we realize that nothing can stop us, and what is really important.

We have to fix both the goal and the way. The goal: our *ratzon* (will) should be only for G-d. The way: we need not be affected by the limitations of the *hishtalshelus*, since they are all there to help us connect to G-d, so they cannot stop us. As said at the start of chapter 12, that is why understanding this lets you direct your *ratzon* to G-d Himself, *v'dai l'mevin*.

reviewQuestions.question: What does it mean that the light of the Essence is still there after the *tzimtzum*, and why is it impossible not to see G-d?
How is a person's taste different from his wish for ice cream, and what does that show about the light of the Essence and our world?
By the *mashal* of the soul in the body, why is the *tzimtzum* not a change in G-d, even though the light after it is connected to the world?
Why is the short version that includes the whole length not a true likeness for the *reshimu*, and what does the thrown stone add?
G-d will not forget or deviate, so why does the *mashal* of the craftsman's blueprint apply to Him?
What is a "born light", and how do the curtain and the glowing metal explain it?

notes.text: Line 13 ("v'zehu ata hu kulei v'kayadua") is not read in any class; it has a no-recording passage. Class 30 goes from line 12 straight to line 14, though its explanation of line 11 (30 w1117-1313) already covers "ata hu".

Line 8: he gives "yashes choshech sisro" as Tehillim chapter 19 (30 w789-793); the verse is Psalms 18:12. Kept as he said it. The saying "b'reisha chashocha" he attributes to the Gemara and links to the goats walking ahead of the lambs (Shabbos 77b, as he gives it). Its phrase cites his explanation a few sentences after the reading (30 w840-849), since he gives no rendering at the reading itself.

Phrases that cite a sentence away from the reading: line 14's second half is read at the end of class 30 and rendered at the start of class 31 (31 w7-24); line 22's "v'im kol ze lo yishtane" cites his "and on the other hand" (31 w1294-1308); line 42's rendering comes after line 41 (32 w636-650), where he first reads it, though the alignment marks his second reading at 32 w790; line 47's end cites 32 w1476-1485, after the reading at w1461; line 64 cites his answer to "why did he make it?" (33 w940-961); line 67 cites the end of his halacha example (33 w1302-1325); line 59's second half and line 60 share one sentence (33 w600-639), split at "within Himself"; line 24's "v'im kol ze b'tzimtzum ha'or bivchinas haKav" cites his "even though it comes in a measured way" (31 w1461-1468), said right after he reads it with the rest of the line (reviewer's addition). Line 46's "hane'lam" is cut with the phrase after it, as he reads and renders it ("which is hidden within them").

Phrases read without English: line 5's "k'mo shekasuv b'Etz Chaim", line 18's "v'chahai gavna", line 20's "v'dai l'mevin", all of line 25 (transcribed as "mikoach hatinok", the machine's hearing of "hatnua"), the end of line 26, line 27, the end of line 38 and line 49, line 52's "kanizkar l'eil", line 53's "v'dai l'mevin", "aval" at the end of line 55, and line 79, whose only English (34 w1872-2023) is an explanation, not a rendering. Line 4's last phrase and line 50's last phrase cite renderings that are looser than the words.

Garbled stretches folded into blocks without their unclear words: 31 w1450-1536 ("if something is holy it will reveal G-d more, and if it's the revelation will go away"), rendered as "the revelation can go away"; 33 w1479-1507 ("should not, that should not happen"), left out of the block's text; 30 w363-368 ("It's not there, it's still here"), rendered as "It has not gone somewhere else".

Sensitivity: no block is flagged. Considered and left unflagged: "that's the whole thing of avoda zara" (32 w2109-2132), a Torah point about perceiving the world as separate from G-d that names no group; the remark that Kabbala looks to many people like a machine (34 w133-229), criticism of an impression, not of a group; the eye doctor on mivtzaim and the student who wants to be an architect, both unnamed; and the Rebbe Rashab's oath, a story told about a Rebbe with reverence.
